name: Bread from Milk Yeast
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: corn meal
ingredients.originalText: half a cup of corn meal

ingredients.name: pint and a half of warm water
ingredients.originalText: pint and a half of warm water

instructions.text: At noon the day before baking, take half a cup of corn meal and pour over it enough sweet milk boiling hot to make it the thickness of batter-cakes
In the winter place it where it will keep warm
The next morning before breakfast pour into a pitcher a pint of boiling water
add one teaspoonful of soda and one of salt
When cool enough so that it will not scald the flour, add enough to make a stiff batter
add the cup of meal set the day before
place the pitcher in a kettle of warm water, cover the top with a folded towel and put it where it will keep warm
Then pour the yeast into a bread-pan
add a pint and a half of warm water, or half water and half milk, and flour enough to knead into loaves
Knead but little harder than for biscuit and bake as soon as it rises to the top of the tin
Do not allow it to get too light before baking, for it will make the bread dry and crumbling

source.originalInstructions:
1. At noon the day before baking, take half a cup of corn meal and pour over it enough sweet milk boiling hot to make it the thickness of batter-cakes
2. In the winter place it where it will keep warm
3. The next morning before breakfast pour into a pitcher a pint of boiling water
4. add one teaspoonful of soda and one of salt
5. When cool enough so that it will not scald the flour, add enough to make a stiff batter
6. add the cup of meal set the day before
7. place the pitcher in a kettle of warm water, cover the top with a folded towel and put it where it will keep warm
8. Then pour the yeast into a bread-pan
9. add a pint and a half of warm water, or half water and half milk, and flour enough to knead into loaves
10. Knead but little harder than for biscuit and bake as soon as it rises to the top of the tin
11. Do not allow it to get too light before baking, for it will make the bread dry and crumbling
